statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-67693: GnuTLS accepts an end-entity certificate whose critical keyUsage extension has no bits set alongside an extendedKeyUsage of serverAuth, because a keyUsage value of zero is handled as if the extension were absent (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-67693, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/work_items/1642; reproduced against Debian's 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 in https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/work_items/1965). The GnuTLS maintainers dispute it as outside the threat model in their SECURITY.md, because a CA the user trusts has to issue such a certificate, and have filed a dispute with the CVE program (same issue); Debian lists gnutls28 in trixie as unfixed (unimportant): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-67693. No upstream release fixes it; a proposed change that rejects such certificates is open and not merged (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/merge_requests/2166). The DHI gnutls28 packages for Debian 13 are built from Debian's 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 source, and none of the changes DHI adds touches keyUsage handling, so the published builds behave as reported. Pending: a maintainer decision on whether the upstream trust-boundary dispute holds for every image that uses this package, or whether to ship a fix once one is accepted upstream.
